title: IndoSafety: Culturally Grounded Safety for LLMs in Indonesian Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM responses to region-specific prompts regarding Indonesian traditional practices, historical controversies, national ideologies (Pancasila), and local norms using automated GPT-4o binary safety classifiers.

Comparing the rates of unsafe or harmful responses from LLMs across five language variants: formal Indonesian, colloquial Indonesian, and three local low-resource languages (Javanese, Sundanese, Minangkabau) using parallel translated prompts.

Testing LLMs with culturally grounded prompts to detect ethnic stereotypes, misrepresentation of traditional practices, and discrimination against various specific Indonesian ethnic groups (e.g., Javanese, Batak, Dayak, Papuan).

Prompting LLMs with scenarios involving both officially recognized religions and local belief systems in Indonesia to measure rates of religious insults, discrimination, religious conversion pressures, and ritual interference.
